citation.title: Designing a TPMS metamaterial via deep learning and topology optimization
citation.authors: Asha Viswanath, Diab W. Abueidda, Mohamad Modrek, Rashid K. Abu Al-Rub, Seid Koric, Kamran A. Khan

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The authors present a CNN that predicts optimized gyroid unit-cell geometries nearly instantly as a lower-cost alternative to repeated 3D topology optimization.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No ML-versus-classical end-to-end speed-up factor is reported. Introduction reports about 67 s for one 32×32×32 SIMP iteration and 200–800 iterations to converge, while Table 2 gives ML prediction as 0.001 CPU hours; these are not a matched total-runtime comparison.
claim.alternatives: Introduction: one 32×32×32 classical optimization iteration takes approximately 67 s and convergence may require approximately 200–800 iterations; conclusion describes an accelerated design workflow.

baseline.classical_method: 3D homogenization-based density SIMP topology optimization; maximize bulk or shear modulus
baseline.implementation: Modified MATLAB homogenization TO code (based on Gao et al.); CNN in Python/Keras with TensorFlow
baseline.hardware_classical: IBM HPC: two 12-core Intel Xeon E5-2695 v2 CPUs, two NVIDIA K20M GPUs, 264 GB memory; iForge HPC: Intel/Skylake nodes, 40 cores and 192 GB RAM, some with NVIDIA V100 GPUs (Section 3.2)
baseline.hardware_ml: CNN hardware not tied to prediction; training on HPC (Section 3.2)
baseline.classical_iterations: Convergence generally approximately 200–800 iterations (Introduction); some parameter cases discarded after 1,000 iterations (Section 5)
baseline.classical_time: Approximately 67 s per iteration on a workstation for a 32×32×32 mesh (Introduction); data generation 24 CPU hours total over HPC allocations (Table 2)
baseline.ml_time: Prediction: 0.001 CPU hours (Table 2); described as nearly instantaneous in Section 3.2
baseline.data_generation_cost: 24 CPU hours on HPC for 2,751 data points; estimated 2.4 h for each data point on one core (Section 3.2 and Table 2)
baseline.quality_metric: MSE, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), and predicted volume deviation (Sections 3.3, 5)
baseline.quality_gap: Test-set MSE 0.0079; mean predicted-volume deviation 0.24%; mean DSC about 95% (Section 5)

R1.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 5 compare predicted topology images with ground-truth SIMP images and report MSE/DSC and volume deviation, but no matched-time or objective/compliance comparison is made; classical convergence is not matched to CNN output quality.

R2.evidence: Sections 2–3 identify the MATLAB SIMP comparator and report HPC hardware, but no evidence establishes an inefficient solver, excessive iteration count, abstract understatement, or an unmatched CPU/GPU comparison.

R3.evidence: Section 3.2 and Table 2 report 24 CPU hours for data generation, 5.5 GPU hours for training, and 0.001 CPU hours for prediction; no break-even use count or explicit per-query-only qualification is given.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 5 validate predicted output primarily by image similarity (MSE/DSC); the returned CNN designs are not reported as FE-verified, and failures are excluded from the dataset rather than counted as model failure rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: 2,751 generated cases; 2,597 bulk-modulus and 2,741 shear-modulus data cases retained; 90%/5%/5% train/validation/test split (Section 5)

notes: The authors state that non-converged parameter combinations and hollow or undesirable designs were discarded (Section 5); the number of failed cases is not tabulated. Public MATLAB/Python code is linked, but no code license permitting a retest is stated in the article.
